subject.title: Browser backend plugin interface (support third-party drivers via MCP/custom adapter)

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic browser backend Plugin SDK/registry seam for third-party drivers, or keep browser backends limited to first-party profile drivers for now?
rationale: This is a public API, config, runtime dispatch, and browser-control security boundary; automation can verify the missing seam but cannot safely choose the permanent extension contract.

options.title: Design generic SDK registry
options.body: Add a versioned backend contract, registry-owned driver ids, config/schema/client/runtime routing, docs, and security tests before accepting third-party adapters.

options.title: Keep first-party drivers only
options.body: Handle Browserbase, My Browser, relay, and similar needs as individual built-in or bundled-plugin drivers without exposing a generic third-party contract yet.

options.title: Defer until narrower work settles
options.body: Keep this issue open while the narrower browser-driver PRs clarify the minimum safe registration API.

recommendation.title: Design generic SDK registry
recommendation.body: Add a versioned backend contract, registry-owned driver ids, config/schema/client/runtime routing, docs, and security tests before accepting third-party adapters.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the freshest merged work on the browser driver surface and authored the prior review framing this as a Plugin SDK design gap.
